## Precipitation and evaporation kinetics in the example drivers (driver-level coupling) {#sec-ch10-kinetics}

The snapy library does not run reaction kinetics. Two example drivers do: `examples/run_hydro.cpp` and
`examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp`. After all RK stages of a step, they refresh the primitive state, evaluate
kintera's rates and their Jacobian at the post-step state, take one linearised implicit step for the
concentrations, add the change to the species rows of the conserved state and call `check_redo`. The coupling is
therefore operator-split, first order, and a property of those drivers: a run built on the library alone has no
kinetics unless its own driver adds the same block. As with the saturation adjustment, latent heat is carried by
the reference energies, so the energy row is not touched.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Advances the species by one linearised backward-Euler step of kintera's rates between steps; @eq-ch10-kinetics-step.

**Data.** Reads $T$, $p$[^rg-be92f09ac0a7] and molar concentrations of the post-step state; writes the species rows, ghosts included.

**Placement.** In the example drivers, after all RK stages of a step and before `check_redo`.

**Activation.** No library switch: only drivers that build a kintera `Kinetics` from the card's reactions.

**Guarantee / limits.** First order, operator-split; never overshoots equilibrium for a linear law; no exchange after.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch10-kinetics-tests; `test_uranus_cycle1_abort.release`, `kinetics_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C12]`.
:::

Local symbols: $\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}$ is the vector of reaction rates [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$] and
$\mathsf J_{\dot\omega}$ its Jacobian with respect to the molar concentrations, at fixed temperature; the subscript
keeps it apart from the $\mathsf J$ of the phase solve in @sec-ch02-saturation. For an evaporation reaction $k$,
$c(k)$ is its condensate, $\nu^{+}_k$ its number of gaseous products (one or two), $\zeta_k$[^rg-a701b5051405] [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$] its
extent to saturation (a reaction extent per volume, as in @sec-ch02-saturation), $K_{p,k}$ [$\mathrm{Pa}^{\nu^{+}_k}$] the equilibrium product of the gas partial pressures,
$\Gamma_k$ [$\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$] its rate coefficient, $D_k$ [$\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$] the diffusivity of
its gases, $V_{\mathrm m,k}$ [$\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$] the molar volume of the condensate (roman m, not the cell
volume $V_i$) and $d_{\mathrm p,k}$ [m] the particle diameter.

### Derivation

Why the update is one linearised backward-Euler step:

1. *Evaluate once.* The rates are evaluated once, at the concentrations $\tilde{\mathbf c}$ of the step's end.
2. *Backward Euler.* One step of $\mathrm{d}\tilde{\mathbf c}/\mathrm{d}t=\mathsf N\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}(\tilde{\mathbf c})$ is
   $\tilde{\mathbf c}+\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c}=\tilde{\mathbf c}+\Delta t\,\mathsf N\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}(\tilde{\mathbf c}+\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c})$.
3. *Linearise.* $\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}(\tilde{\mathbf c}+\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c})\approx\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}+\mathsf J_{\dot\omega}\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c}$;
   dividing by $\Delta t$ gives

$$
\Big(\frac{\mathsf I}{\Delta t}-\mathsf N\mathsf J_{\dot\omega}\Big)\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c} = \mathsf N\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}
$$ {#eq-ch10-kinetics-step}

for the change $\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c}$ over the step $\Delta t$. @eq-ch10-kinetics-step is assembled in
kintera's `evolve_implicit_cell` as the matrix `A`, with `inv_dt` on its diagonal, and the right-hand side `sr`
([`kintera evolve_implicit_impl.h:66-71`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evolve_implicit_impl.h#L66-L71)), and solved by LU[^rg-a5613ad1789f] with
partial pivoting, falling back to a minimum-norm least-squares solve for a singular cell, `dsolve_lu`
([`kintera evolve_implicit_impl.h:77`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evolve_implicit_impl.h#L77)).
For a linear rate law the step is exactly backward Euler (`[C2]`).[^kin-c]

4. *No overshoot.* For the reversible linear reaction $A\rightleftharpoons B$ with rate constants $k_{\mathrm f}$,
   $k_{\mathrm b}$ [s$^{-1}$] the step moves the distance to equilibrium by the factor $1/(1+\Delta t(k_{\mathrm f}+k_{\mathrm b}))$,
   which lies in $(0,1]$ for every $\Delta t$: one step never overshoots equilibrium, however large the step
   (`[C3]`; `[C10]` derives the factor with sympy).
5. *Zero net mass.* The driver converts the change to partial densities, $\Delta\rho_n=\mu_n\Delta\tilde c_n$; for a
   mass-balanced reaction $\sum_n\mu_n\nu_{nk}=0$, so the update has zero net mass (`[C4]`; `[C11]` for
   $\mathrm{NH_4SH(s)}\to\mathrm{NH_3}+\mathrm{H_2S}$).
6. *Round-off of the mass.* Each $\Delta\rho_n$ is one division (by the stored inverse molar mass), so the net mass of
   an update is zero to about $N_y\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\max_n\lvert\mu_n\Delta\tilde c_n\rvert$; `[C4]` measures
   $2.1\times10^{-15}$ of that maximum over 100 random steps.

An evaporation reaction $k$ has one reactant, its condensate $c(k)$, and one or two gaseous products, all with
coefficient 1; kintera refuses any other form, and with products counted positive in $\mathsf N$[^rg-8d1709112bc8],
$\nu_{c(k)k}=-1$ (the check `unit_reactant`, [`kintera evaporation.cpp:82-96`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp#L82-L96);
the matrix `stoich_base`, [`kintera kinetics.cpp:105-120`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp#L105-L120)).
Its equilibrium constant is the product of the saturation concentrations of its gases over the pure condensate,

$$
K_k=\frac{K_{p,k}(T)}{(\mathcal RT)^{\nu^{+}_k}}\quad[\mathrm{mol}^{\nu^{+}_k}\,\mathrm m^{-3\nu^{+}_k}],
$$ {#eq-ch10-kinetics-K}

with $K_{p,k}=p_{\mathrm{sat},k}(T)$ [Pa] for one gas and the equilibrium product of the two partial pressures
[$\mathrm{Pa^2}$] for two, read from the reaction's saturation function on the card; it depends on $T$ only (`[C6]` checks the form). It is
`ksat`
([`kintera evaporation.cpp:148-154`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp#L148-L154));
for $\mathrm{NH_4SH}$ the card's `nh3_h2s_lewis` returns $\ln K_{p,k}$ in $\mathrm{Pa^2}$
([`kintera vapor_functions.h:81-82`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/vapors/vapor_functions.h#L81-L82)).

Why the rate law has the factor 12:

1. *One particle.* A sphere of diameter $d_{\mathrm p,k}$ whose surface holds a gas at $\tilde c_{n,s}$, in still gas at
   $\tilde c_n$[^rg-bbb838859464], loses $2\pi d_{\mathrm p,k}D_k(\tilde c_{n,s}-\tilde c_n)$ moles per second (steady diffusion).
2. *Number of particles.* The condensate fills the volume fraction $\tilde c_{c(k)}V_{\mathrm m,k}$, so there are
   $\tilde c_{c(k)}V_{\mathrm m,k}/(\pi d_{\mathrm p,k}^3/6)$ monodisperse particles per unit volume.
3. *Multiply.* The rate per unit volume is the product, $2\pi d D\cdot6V_{\mathrm m}\tilde c_{c(k)}/(\pi d^3)\,\zeta_k
   =12DV_{\mathrm m}\tilde c_{c(k)}\zeta_k/d^2$ (`[C5]`, sympy):

$$
\dot\omega_k=\Gamma_k\,\tilde c_{c(k)}\,\zeta_k,\qquad
\Gamma_k=\frac{12\,D_k\,V_{\mathrm m,k}}{d_{\mathrm p,k}^2},\qquad
D_k=D_{0,k}\Big(\frac{T}{T_{\mathrm{ev}}}\Big)^{\alpha_{T,k}}\Big(\frac{p}{p_{\mathrm{ev}}}\Big)^{\alpha_{p,k}},
$$ {#eq-ch10-kinetics-rate}

@eq-ch10-kinetics-rate is `kappa`
([`kintera evaporation.cpp:142-145`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp#L142-L145))
times the mass-action factor `rate_f`
([`kintera kinetics.cpp:420-423`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp#L420-L423));
`[C5]` re-derives the factor 12 and `[C6]` the form of $K_k$[^rg-cd51099e912b].

Here $\zeta_k=\tilde c_{n,s}-\tilde c_n$ is the excess of the gas at the surface over the air far away. With the surface
at saturation, one gas gives $\zeta_k=K_k-\tilde c_n$. For two gases, $AB(s)\to A+B$, the solid dissolves congruently, so
both gases leave at the same molar rate and both carry the same excess $\zeta_k$, and the surface equilibrium
$(\tilde c_A+\zeta_k)(\tilde c_B+\zeta_k)=K_k$ fixes it: $\zeta_k$ is the root of
$\zeta_k^2+(\tilde c_A+\tilde c_B)\zeta_k-(K_k-\tilde c_A\tilde c_B)=0$ that keeps both surface concentrations positive (`[C7]`).
Multiplying that root by its conjugate, with
$(\tilde c_A-\tilde c_B)^2+4K_k-(\tilde c_A+\tilde c_B)^2=4(K_k-\tilde c_A\tilde c_B)$, gives a form without
cancellation,

$$
\zeta_k = \frac{2\,(K_k-\tilde c_A\tilde c_B)}{\tilde c_A+\tilde c_B+\sqrt{(\tilde c_A-\tilde c_B)^2+4K_k}},
$$ {#eq-ch10-kinetics-extent}

whose sign is that of $K_k-\tilde c_A\tilde c_B$. In both cases $\zeta_k$ is the extent of evaporation that would bring
the air to saturation at fixed $T$, and the code sets it to zero where the air is already saturated, so this law only
evaporates; condensate grows only through the saturation adjustment (@sec-ch10-satadj). $\Gamma_k$ is `kappa` and
$\zeta_k$ is `eta`, with the two-product root as `x` and its square root as `root`
([`kintera evaporation.cpp:142-194`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp#L142-L194));
the factor $\tilde c_{c(k)}$ is kintera's mass-action product over the one reactant, `rate_f`
([`kintera kinetics.cpp:420-423`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp#L420-L423)).
The card sets $D_{0,k}$, $\alpha_{T,k}$, $\alpha_{p,k}$, $V_{\mathrm m,k}$ and $d_{\mathrm p,k}$ as `diff_c`[^rg-78e31ef7a580], `diff_T`[^rg-887c534d4646],
`diff_P`[^rg-3ce607edb974], `vm`[^rg-153a31353848] and `diameter`[^rg-03f9c553417b] (defaults $2\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$, 1.75, $-1$,
$1.8\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, $10^{-2}$ m); the reference state $T_{\mathrm{ev}}=300$ K,
$p_{\mathrm{ev}}=10^5$ Pa is a default the card reader never sets (the card values from
`diff_c` on, [`kintera evaporation.cpp:50-57`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp#L50-L57); the constants `Tref` and `Pref`,
[`kintera evaporation.hpp:54-73`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.hpp#L54-L73)).
Ventilation, the Kelvin effect and kinetic corrections to the diffusion flux are not in the law.

The Jacobian of @eq-ch10-kinetics-step holds the temperature fixed:
$(\mathsf J_{\dot\omega})_{kn}=\tilde c_{c(k)}\,\partial(\Gamma_k\zeta_k)/\partial\tilde c_n+[n=c(k)]\,\Gamma_k\zeta_k$,
where $[n=c(k)]$ is 1 for the condensate's own column and 0 otherwise (the mass-action term, `[C12]`),
with $\partial \zeta_k/\partial\tilde c_n=-1$ for one gas and
$\partial \zeta_k/\partial\tilde c_A=-(\tilde c_B+\zeta_k)/(\tilde c_A+\tilde c_B+2\zeta_k)$ (`[C9]`) for two (and likewise for $B$), zero
where $\zeta_k$ is clamped. kintera forms the first term by automatic differentiation and the second as the mass-action
term, `jac`
([`kintera kinetics.cpp:306-310`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp#L306-L310));
its temperature term enters only with `evolve_temperature`, false by default and set by neither the card nor the
drivers
([`kintera kinetics.hpp:73`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp#L73)).
`[C1]` and `[C8]` show that @eq-ch10-kinetics-extent is the root that keeps both surface concentrations positive.

[^kin-c]: Printed round-off digits, including `[C4]`, depend on the environment; the assertions define the thresholds.
    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch10/checks/kinetics_check.py`, output `kinetics_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C12]`; a
    numpy and sympy port of kintera's `evolve_implicit_cell` and `EvaporationImpl::forward` at
    `c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77` and of the species update of `examples/run_hydro.cpp` at the snapy
    pin, double precision.
    Run on CPU, one process, with Python 3.12.10, sympy 1.14.0 and numpy 2.5.3; the output matches the committed file.

### Numerical method

The block runs once per accepted or attempted step, after the stages and before `check_redo`
({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
It first recomputes `hydro_w` from `hydro_u`, so the rates see the saturation-adjusted state
({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
It acts on the whole array, ghosts included, with no exchange; the next stage's boundary fill and exchange restore
consistency. No conserved limiter writes `hydro_u` between the update and `check_redo`. With `limiter: true` the
floor test of `check_redo` converts a copy of the state with the equation of state, and that conversion runs the
conserved limiter on the copy (`_cons2prim` of each moist equation of state calls `apply_conserved_limiter_`), so a
negative species the kinetics produced is repaired on the copy, sets the limiter mark if the repair is above
round-off, and redoes the step with cause 4 in the same check
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). Without the limiter the negative
species stays in the state. @fig-ch10-kinetics-extent compares
the extent law with the plain law $K_k-\tilde c_A\tilde c_B$, the drive `eta` that kintera forms for every
reaction before it replaces the two-product ones by the extent.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-kinetics-extent
#| fig-cap: "Evaporation drive of a two-product condensate against the saturation ratio, each curve divided by its value at zero saturation. Green: the extent law, solid for equal gas concentrations, dashed for one gas ten times the other; blue dotted: the plain law $K-\\tilde c_A\\tilde c_B$ for the same gases. The extent law falls faster near zero saturation, and depends on how the product is split between the gases."
#| fig-alt: "Three decreasing curves from 1 at saturation ratio 0 to 0 at ratio 1; the two extent curves lie below the straight dotted line."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch10.figures.fig_kinetics_extent import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

Run kinetics with `build/bin/run_hydro.release` or `build/bin/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.release`; a library-only dynamics call does not execute these driver updates.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| kinetics block | {{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}} | `evolve_implicit` | driver |
| redo after kinetics | {{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}} | `check_redo` | |
| same, 1-D driver | {{< code examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.cpp main >}} | `evolve_implicit` | driver |
| implicit step | [`kintera evolve_implicit_impl.h:55-77`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evolve_implicit_impl.h#L55-L77) | `evolve_implicit_cell` | |
| evaporation rate | [`kintera evaporation.cpp:128-195`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp#L128-L195) | `EvaporationImpl::forward` | |

: Code map of the driver-level kinetics. {#tbl-ch10-kinetics-code}

1. Refresh the primitives from the adjusted conserved state, `hydro_w` ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
2. Form temperature, pressure and concentrations, `conc` ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
3. Evaluate rates and Jacobian, `jacobian` ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
4. Take the implicit step and convert to densities, `del_rho` ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
5. Add to the species rows of `hydro_u` ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
6. Accept, redo or terminate, `check_redo` ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).

**How to use it.** The library has no switch. A driver that builds kintera's `Kinetics` from the card runs the block,
and the card lists evaporation reactions with their rate law
({{< code examples/jupiter_evap_precip_1d.yaml >}}):

```yaml
reactions:
  - equation: NH4SH(s,p) => NH3 + H2S
    type: evaporation
    rate-constant: {formula: nh3_h2s_lewis, diff_c: 0.2e-4, diff_T: 1.75, diff_P: -1.,
                    vm: 43.e-6, diameter: 1.0e-4}
```

Refused: an evaporation reaction that is reversible, or has more than one reactant, or not one or two products, or
a coefficient other than 1, with "Evaporation reaction '…' must be irreversible with one reactant and one or two
products, each with stoichiometric coefficient 1", because the rate law of steps 1 to 3 assumes exactly that
(`unit_reactant`, [`kintera evaporation.cpp:82-96`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp#L82-L96)).
The block of @eq-ch10-kinetics-step, with the conversion $\Delta\rho_n=\mu_n\Delta\tilde c_n$, is these lines
({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}):

```cpp
    auto [rate, rc_ddC, rc_ddT, rate_constants] =
        kinet->forward_with_rate_constants(temp, pres, conc_kinet);
    auto jac = kinet->jacobian(temp, conc_kinet, cp_vol, rate, rc_ddC, rc_ddT,
                               rate_constants);
    auto del_conc = kintera::evolve_implicit(rate, kinet->stoich, jac, dt);
    ...
    auto del_rho = del_conc / thermo_y->inv_mu.narrow(0, 1, ny).view(vec);
    hydro_u.narrow(0, ICY, ny) += del_rho.permute({3, 0, 1, 2});
```

`rate` is $\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}$, `rate_constants` are the raw coefficients $\Gamma_k\zeta_k$ of the same call, which
`jacobian` takes as the mass-action term (kintera requires them where a condensate is zero; kintera $\ge$ 2.6.3), `jac` is
$\mathsf J_{\dot\omega}$, `evolve_implicit` solves @eq-ch10-kinetics-step for
`del_conc` $=\Delta\tilde{\mathbf c}$, and the last two lines are step 5. A driver of one's own copies these lines
between the stages and `check_redo`.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_uranus_cycle1_abort.release` | column reaches cycle 40, no redo | exit status | log strings |

: Tests of the driver-level kinetics; it passes at the pin (@tbl-ch10-ctest-run). {#tbl-ch10-kinetics-tests}

`UranusLate.column_reaches_cycle_40` runs `run_hydro` on a Uranus column and requires exit code 0, no "Redoing the
step" and no "Terminating abnormally" in the log
({{< code tests/test_uranus_cycle1_abort.cpp UranusLate.column_reaches_cycle_40 >}}).
Its ctest, `test_uranus_cycle1_abort.release`, is the only snapy test that runs the kinetics block. Its two other
cases run `run_hydro` as well and check only how the run ends: `UranusCycle1.column_finishes_the_two_cycles` on a
Uranus deck with nucleation, coagulation and evaporation reactions, and `abnormal_termination_exits_nonzero` on a
floor deck ({{< code tests/test_uranus_cycle1_abort.cpp UranusCycle1.column_finishes_the_two_cycles >}},
{{< code tests/test_uranus_cycle1_abort.cpp UranusCycle1.abnormal_termination_exits_nonzero >}}; both through
`run_deck`, {{< code tests/test_uranus_cycle1_abort.cpp run_deck >}}). There is no snapy test of one kinetics step's mass and
energy budget, of the evaporation rate or of `jupiter_evap_precip_1d`: **missing evidence** on the snapy side; the
rate law is tested in kintera. CPU only; no CUDA or multi-rank arm.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Kinetics exists only in drivers that implement it. A user driver that calls only `forward` and `check_redo` has none.
:::

- First order in time, operator-split from the dynamics; the split error is not measured.
- No conserved limiter writes the state between the update and `check_redo`. With the limiter on, a negative
  species from the kinetics is caught on the copy the floor test converts and redoes the step (cause 4); a deficit
  of round-off size is repaired without a mark and so is not redone (@sec-ch10-redo). With the limiter off it stays in the state.
- The update covers ghosts without an exchange.
- `sources/canoe__EVAPORATION_MULTIPRODUCT_TECH_REPORT.md` describes the extent law as not yet in kintera; it is
  present at the kintera pin (@eq-ch10-kinetics-extent).
- Not in the switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix).

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-be92f09ac0a7]: $p$ — pressure [Pa]

[^rg-a701b5051405]: $\zeta_k$ — equilibrium concentration shift for reaction $k$, distinct from local sponge/profile coordinates [mol m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-a5613ad1789f]: LU — lower–upper matrix factorisation

[^rg-8d1709112bc8]: $\mathsf N$ — the stoichiometry matrix, $\mathsf N_{nk} = \nu_{nk}$, species by reaction; never $\mathsf S$, which is the centroid-slope matrix (§4)

[^rg-bbb838859464]: $\tilde c_n$ — molar concentration of species $n$ [mol m$^{-3}$]; the tilde separates it from the specific heats $c_{v,n}, c_{p,n}$ and the sound speed $c_s$

[^rg-cd51099e912b]: $K_k$ — equilibrium constant of reaction $k$ [units stated per reaction]; never $K_f$, a face diffusion coefficient (§8), and never $\mathcal K$, the curvature flux (§3); [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/equilibrium/phase_equilibrate_tp.h#L16-L35)

[^rg-78e31ef7a580]: diff_c — reference diffusivity in the reaction-rate model

[^rg-887c534d4646]: diff_T — temperature exponent of the diffusivity

[^rg-3ce607edb974]: diff_P — pressure exponent of the diffusivity

[^rg-153a31353848]: vm — molar volume used by the reaction-rate model

[^rg-03f9c553417b]: diameter — particle diameter used by the reaction-rate model
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
